sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 46.6% a year from $6.91 billion in FY2017 to $215.9 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F211].
The path was not smooth: FY2023 revenue was flat at 0.2% growth and operating margin fell 21.6pp to 15.7% [D284][D299][F47].
That trough came from $2.17 billion of inventory provisions against excess Ampere supply, particularly for expected demand in China [P35][P38].
The recovery was a step change: revenue rose 125.9% in FY2024 and 114.2% in FY2025, driven by data center compute and networking for accelerated computing and AI [D338][D393][P10][P16].
FY2026 growth slowed to 65.5%, with Data Center contributing 60.2pp [D448][D622].
Data Center grew from 19.9% of revenue in FY2018 to 89.7% in FY2026, contributing 60.2pp of FY2026's 65.5% growth [D598][D620][D622][D448].
Within it, Data Center computing grew 59% on Blackwell demand and networking grew 142% on NVLink for GB200 and GB300 systems [P8].
Networking contributed 14.1pp in FY2026 against 46.1pp from Compute, so the largest driver remains concentrated in one product line [D636][D629].
Operating income grew 60.1% against 65.5% revenue growth, an incremental margin of 57.3% [D449][D448][D475].
Diluted EPS grew 66.7% against 64.7% net income growth as the diluted share count fell 1.2% [D452][D450][D470].
Operating margin of 60.4% in FY2026 sits well above the 32.8% window median but below the 62.4% FY2025 high [F50][D813][D812].
Gross margin fell 3.9pp to 71.1% and drove the 2.0pp operating-margin decline, partly offset by R&D and SG&A leverage of 1.3pp and 0.6pp [F30][D462][D463][D478][D479].
The FY2026 Compute & Networking operating-income increase was partly offset by a $4.5 billion H20 excess-inventory and purchase-obligation charge [P7].
Operating expenses rose 41%, driven by compensation and benefits from employee growth and by compute and infrastructure costs [P9][P5].
Net margin held at 55.6% because other income of $11.1 billion, largely unrealized equity gains including Intel, offset a tax rate rising to 15.1% [F70][X120][P3][D434][P2].
Operating cash flow of $102.7 billion was 0.86x net income, below the 1.00x of FY2017, and free cash flow was 0.81x, the window low [F100][F60][D435][D8][D436][D826].
Free cash flow margin of 44.8% is near the 44.4% window median, with capex at 2.8% of revenue and 2.13x D&A [D432][D822][D431][D437].
Inventory grew 112.3% and receivables 66.8%, pushing days inventory to 125 and days sales outstanding to 65 [D474][D473][D446][D445].
Stock-based compensation of $6.4 billion was only 6.2% of operating cash flow, so conversion is diluted by working capital rather than non-cash add-backs [X80][D438].
Net cash fell to $2.1 billion, just 1.0% of revenue, from $34.7 billion a year earlier, as cash and investments dropped 75.5% to $10.6 billion [D441][D442][D386][D471][D439].
Investing outflow of $52.2 billion rose on higher equity investment purchases and a non-exclusive license agreement with Groq [F120][P1].
Net cash still ranks in the 83rd percentile of six semis peers against a median of -13.9% of revenue, and the current ratio is 3.91x [D844][D845][F190].
Buybacks and dividends of $41.1 billion absorbed 42.5% of free cash flow, and long-term debt fell 11.7% to $7.5 billion [D443][D444][F200][D459].
Customer concentration is the main risk: two direct customers were 22% and 14% of FY2026 revenue, both mainly in Compute & Networking [P6].
China revenue fell 21.4% in FY2026, subtracting 4.1pp from growth, after contributing 20.9pp in FY2025 [D545][D546][D543].
The Graphics segment's 25% FY2023 decline was a one-period cyclical event, with segment revenue up 57.0% in FY2026, so it is not a persistent flag [D754][D747].
Product revenue members sum to 190% of consolidated revenue in FY2026 because some are totals of others, so segment shares must not be added [R2].
Gross margin: a further move below the 71.1% of FY2026 would confirm cost pressure from the H20 charge and product mix, reported in the FY2027 10-K [F30][P7].
Data Center share: holding above the 89.7% of FY2026 confirms the concentration trend, while a fall toward the 78.0% of FY2024 would signal broadening [D620][D614].
Free cash flow conversion: a ratio below the 0.81x window low of FY2026 would show working capital outgrowing earnings [D436][D826].
